newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi shares extend losses on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi shares extend losses on profit-taking.

text.p: Increased selling pressure at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) continued to push prices down on Friday, bourse officials said.

"Most investors are now cashing in on quick profits made on the high prices seen in the last two weeks," a bourse official said. "In fact the prices declined at an average of 10 for every three rising."
The NSE 20-share index shed 75.80 points to 3535.00. Turnover was posted at 11.664 million shillings on 269,686 shares from 22.586 million shillings on 451,569 shares.
National carrier Kenya Airways closed at 9.70 from 10.20 while Barclays Bank shed 15.0 to close at 105.
One broker said investors had rushed into the market rather early in anticipation of good end-year results, mainly in the financial sector, which they thought would come out this month.
"But we might see a repeat of what happened in the last two weeks next month because results should be announced around mid-February," another broker said.
Some brokers said that Kenya Airways would continue fluctuating until the share fell into the right hands.
"Kenya Airways has disappointed people for so long that once they saw the price rising they scrambled to sell it -- which made the price go down again," a senior broker said.
Kenya Commercial Bank KCBK.NR eased to 87 from 88 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 50.50 from 57. British American Tobacco (BAT) Kenya closed at 83 from 85.
Sasini Tea & Coffee was unchanged at 75.
Some five million shillings worth of bonds of the East African Development floating-rate bond traded at 104.14 percent.
